title: Signature Strip-Verify Certificates
description: Signature edition: every published artifact carries a strip certificate — what was removed, by which cleaner version, verified by what check. Recipients can confirm the file was cleaned; auditors can sample-verify. Cleanliness becomes checkable, not claimed. This is a Signature original method.
method: Issue certificates per artifact with (removals, cleaner version, verification); attach to the publish record.
usage: Require certificates for external publishes; audit samples independently.

demo.code:
print('artifact report.pdf: strip cert (MAT2 v0.15, 14 fields removed, verified)')
print('recipient verifies cert -> trusts the clean')

title: Signature Document metadata scrubbing
description: Signature edition: Office documents and PDFs hide author names, edit history, comments, and tracked changes — the classic leak (government reports with redacted text recoverable from metadata). Scrubbers remove author info, revision history, and hidden layers before external sharing.
method: Remove author/revision metadata; flatten tracked changes; strip comments and hidden text; verify with a metadata reader.
usage: Scrub every externally-shared document; verify, don't assume; keep the original internally.

demo.code:
print('report.docx: author "J. Smith", 14 revisions, 3 comments')
print('scrubbed: metadata empty, changes accepted, comments removed')

title: Signature PDF redaction verification
description: Signature edition: Fake redaction (black boxes over text) is a famous leak — the text remains underneath. Real redaction removes the text and metadata, and verification tries to extract the 'redacted' content to prove it's gone. The pipeline redacts, then attacks its own output.
method: Remove redacted text (not just cover it); strip metadata; attempt extraction; require zero recoverable content.
usage: Never trust visual redaction; verify by extraction; use proper redaction tools.

demo.code:
print('redacted.pdf: black boxes -> text REMOVED underneath')
print('extraction attack: 0 recoverable chars -> VERIFIED')

title: Signature Video metadata and thumbnail scrubbing
description: Signature edition: Videos hide metadata in container atoms and embedded thumbnails (which can contain their own EXIF, including GPS). Scrubbing removes container metadata and regenerates or strips thumbnails — the preview image shouldn't leak what the video hides.
method: Strip container metadata; handle embedded thumbnails (strip or regenerate); verify with a metadata dump.
usage: Scrub published video; check thumbnails specifically — they're the forgotten leak.

demo.code:
print('video.mp4: 12 metadata atoms removed; thumbnail EXIF (GPS!) stripped')
print('clean: safe to publish')

title: Signature Steganography screening
description: Signature edition: Beyond metadata, files can hide data steganographically (LSB encoding, appended archives). Screening checks for anomalies — unexpected appended data, statistical irregularities — before publishing or ingesting files. It's the deeper clean for high-sensitivity pipelines.
method: Scan for appended data and statistical anomalies; quarantine suspicious files; investigate before release.
usage: Screen inbound files in sensitive pipelines; the check is cheap, the miss is expensive.

demo.code:
print('scan: image.jpg has 2MB appended after EOI marker')
print('QUARANTINED: hidden payload suspected')

title: Signature Publish-pipeline integration
description: Signature edition: Stripping works when it's automatic: the publish pipeline runs the cleaners on every artifact, verifies the output, and blocks publication on failure. Manual stripping is forgotten stripping — the pipeline is the policy.
method: Cleaners as pipeline stages; verification per artifact; block on failure; log what was removed.
usage: Wire stripping into every publish path; no manual exceptions.

demo.code:
print('publish pipeline: 142 artifacts -> cleaned -> verified')
print('3 failed verification -> BLOCKED, fixed, re-run')

title: Signature Audio metadata removal
description: Signature edition: Audio files carry ID3 tags, encoder strings, and sometimes location or device info. Podcasts and published recordings get their tags scrubbed — keep title/artist if intended, remove everything identifying, and re-encode if the container hides data in padding.
method: Strip ID3/all tags; keep only intended fields; check container padding; verify with a tag reader.
usage: Scrub published audio; verify tags after encoding (encoders re-add metadata).

demo.code:
print('episode.mp3: encoder "Lavf", device tag removed')
print('remaining tags: title, artist (intended only)')

title: Signature MAT2 comprehensive cleaner
description: Signature edition: MAT2 (Metadata Anonymisation Toolkit) strips metadata from dozens of formats — images, documents, audio, archives — in one pipeline. It's the standard 'clean everything' tool: point it at a directory before publishing and it handles each format's metadata correctly.
method: Run MAT2 over the publish set; it dispatches per-format cleaners; verify output; integrate into the publish pipeline.
usage: Run MAT2 as a publish gate; update it (new formats, new metadata fields appear).

demo.code:
print('MAT2: 142 files processed (jpg, pdf, docx, mp3)')
print('metadata removed from 138; 4 already clean')

title: Signature Archive and container cleaning
description: Signature edition: Zips and tars carry filenames, timestamps, permissions, and sometimes absolute paths — metadata about the build machine and its user. Cleaning normalizes timestamps (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH), strips paths, and sorts entries, so archives reveal nothing about their origin.
method: Normalize timestamps; strip absolute paths; sort entries; remove owner metadata; verify reproducibility.
usage: Clean all distributed archives; the archive should be reproducible from source alone.

demo.code:
print('release.tar.gz: timestamps -> 1970-01-01, paths relative, sorted')
print('origin metadata: none remaining')
